A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe SplatTalk. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary sections can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original ScanQA, SQA3D, and MSR3D evaluations, sampling and token-length ablations, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations and qualitative examples and reports revised ablation results in Tables 3–4.

M1.justification: The feature autoencoder, joint RGB/language Gaussian training, Gaussian-mean feature extraction, entropy sampling, and optional LoRA remain unchanged. The new token-input discussion explains existing inference rather than establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ScanNet-based ScanQA, SQA3D, and MSR3D coverage. Table 4's change from 'MSQA' to 'MSR3D (test)' corrects the label for the experiment already described as MSR3D.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same benchmark comparators. Table 3 still compares random, point-density, furthest-point, and entropy sampling.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 replaces the sampling ablation's explicit 10-scene subset description with the ScanQA validation set. Table 3 removes the EM@1-R and CIDEr columns and adds Avg. These are localized reported protocol changes; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The same sampling-strategy and token-length questions are retained, with revised sampling evaluation scope and replacement evidence in Tables 3–4. No new robustness tests or qualitative case studies are introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Table 3's new Avg aggregates metrics rather than quantifying experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and qualitative examples are unchanged, but the ablation findings change substantially. Under the revised sampling protocol, entropy no longer leads EM@1: v2 reports 17.1 versus FPS's 17.7. Table 4 replaces MSR3D EM@1 of 11.9/11.9 at 729/32,076 tokens with 7.9/14.1, reversing the previous finding of no token-length benefit.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 condenses the squared-loss and EM analogy while retaining the normalized Gaussian weights and weighted-mean feature expression. The mathematical argument is restated more compactly without a new proof or substantive correction.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about self-supervised zero-shot 3D VQA, Gaussian-mean features, entropy sampling, and competitive benchmark performance.

C2.justification: v2 adds a spatial-grounding explanation for dispensing with explicit positional encodings and fixed token order. Section 4.4 removes the interpretation that SQA3D specifically requires richer context and revises the dataset/model limitations discussion around the new token-length findings.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project website pointer, expands the inherited FreeSplat pipeline description, and explicitly discusses positional encoding and token order. Supplementary architecture, losses, optimizer settings, hardware, and LoRA details remain unchanged; linked resource availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: The same 53 cited works and substantive positioning relative to FreeSplat, LangSplat, and ChatSplat remain. The expanded FreeSplat description explains an already acknowledged dependency without changing the claimed relationship or novelty.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized corrections and rewrites, particularly in the FreeSplat discussion and Section 3.2, and expands Section 3.3 under '3D VQA Inference.' It adds acknowledgments and moves the supplementary sections before the references, renumbering A–D as 6–9.

P2.justification: Table 3 changes its column structure and size, Table 4 corrects its dataset heading, and Tables 1–2 move earlier. Equations become inline and the supplement gains a title block. All five figures retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies architecture and inference, and Table 4's full-length ScanQA/SQA3D results now agree with Table 1. However, revised Table 3 labels entropy's 61.7 as ROUGE, whereas Table 1 reports SplatTalk ROUGE of 32.7 and CIDEr of 61.7, without explaining settings that resolve this discrepancy. These clarity and consistency gains coexist with unresolved ambiguity in the revised ablation reporting, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
